newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks jump on foreign fund buying of banks.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks jump on foreign fund buying of banks.

text.p: Thai stocks gained 2.17 percent by 0758 GMT as foreign funds bought blue chip banking shares actively, traders said.
The SET Index added 15.07 points to 709.81. The SET 50 rose gained 3.36 percent to 53.06 points. Turnover was 2.9 billion baht, sharply up from earlier in the week.

"I think there are some longer term foreign funds nibbling into the banks ... the valuations offer up to 40 percent discounts to other markets in the region," said an analyst at a leading European broker which recently recommended Thai banks.

A number of other major foreign firms have recently advised investors to increase exposure to leading Thai bank stocks over the last two weeks saying the market had fully discounted forthcoming bad news.

The bad news includes a probable downgrade of the country's A2 sovereign credit rating by Moody's Investor Service, slowing economic growth, upward pressure on interest rates, extra provisioning and expectd lower earnings growth, analysts said.

"There is bad news to come but everybody knows it as well. It's difficult to say why it's gaining today but maybe it has taken just a little while to digest the news that the market has discounted," he said.
The bank sector was up 4.39 percent, and recently battered finance stocks were being pulled along, traders said.
Shares of the country's four largest banks, Bangkok Bank Plc, Krung Thai Bank Plc Thai Farmers Bank Plc and Siam Commercial Bank Plc all gaining strongly.
